featured_videos.title: Carnivore Diet for Weight Loss vs Healing: A nuanced chat around finding the right approach
featured_videos.creator: Laura Spath
featured_videos.editorial_title: Carnivore Diet for Weight Loss vs Healing: A nuanced chat around finding the right approach
featured_videos.commentary: Laura's hitting on something the community keeps getting tripped up on, and honestly, it's the biggest source of frustration we see in comments. Weight loss and healing aren't the same goal on carnivore, and trying to use one protocol for both is like showing up to a soccer game with baseball rules. That commenter whose husband needs to lose weight while his wife needs immune healing? That's so many people right now, and they've been fed the same macro recommendation for both situations. The nuance here is real: you might need to actually eat *more* to fix your metabolic foundation, or dial it down strict if you're tracking calories for fat loss. Neither one is wrong. The win is knowing which one you actually need.

featured_videos.title: 200 Days Carnivore | 72 Pounds | 13 1/2 Inches
featured_videos.creator: Butter Bob Briggs
featured_videos.commentary: Butter Bob's comeback is exactly what the community needed right now. Seventy-two pounds in 200 days isn't just a number on a scale, it's proof that consistency beats perfection every single time, and the comments are lit up because people *feel* that. You've got folks saying "I don't even unsubscribe anymore because you never know when someone's going to swing for the fences" and that's the real magic here, right? Bob stepped away, came back stronger, and showed people that this isn't about being perfect or never taking breaks. It's about showing up when it counts. That kind of real-world result, with the specifics about inches lost too, cuts through all the noise about what works and what doesn't on carnivore.

featured_videos.title: Weird Things Carnivore Helps With
featured_videos.creator: Shawn Baker MD
featured_videos.commentary: The responses in this thread are wild because they're not what the mainstream expects to hear. People are reporting stuff like disappearing sunburns, clearer breathing, and stable moods alongside the predictable wins like weight loss and blood sugar control. That's the thing about carnivore that gets buried in the debate. the side effects nobody talks about are often the ones that change someone's life the most. A 70-year-old saying "I have little anxiety" or someone finally sleeping through the night after years of insomnia? Those aren't edge cases. Those are the real reasons people stick with this. The skin improvements, the body odor shift, the respiratory changes. they all point to something deeper happening with inflammation and nutrient density that we're still catching up on understanding.

featured_videos.title: Easy Carnivore Egg Salad Sandwich
featured_videos.creator: Emmathecarnivore
featured_videos.commentary: Emma's nailing what makes carnivore stick for real people: it doesn't have to be complicated or precious. The comments are full of folks swapping sour cream for mayo, air-frying eggs instead of boiling them, and building protein-packed salads they actually want to eat day after day. That's the opposite of restrictive, which is why it works. Simple swaps, real food, zero gatekeeping about the "right" way to do it.

featured_videos.title: Does Protein Really Turn Into Sugar?
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Tony Hampton - The Metabolic Health Doc
featured_videos.editorial_title: Does Protein Really Turn Into Sugar?
featured_videos.commentary: This is the video the carnivore community needed, and Dr. Hampton nailed it. The gluconeogenesis myth has scared a lot of people away from adequate protein, and seeing it broken down this clearly (demand-driven, not supply-driven) should settle that debate once and for all. That said, the comments pointing out individual variation are worth paying attention to. Some people genuinely do see elevated glucose with higher protein intake, and that's where tools like CGM testing become valuable for figuring out your own threshold rather than relying on blanket rules. The takeaway: protein doesn't automatically convert to sugar, but your individual response matters, so test and adjust.

featured_videos.title: This Bean Has Almost NO CARBS… So I Made BBQ Baked Beans With It
featured_videos.creator: Victor Prince
featured_videos.editorial_title: This Bean Has Almost NO CARBS… So I Made BBQ Baked Beans With It
featured_videos.commentary: The "don't eat it if it takes that much work to make it edible" comment hits harder than Victor probably expected, and honestly, it's a fair challenge. Lupini beans do require serious prep to be safe and palatable, which raises the real question: are we solving a problem or creating one? That said, the community feedback shows this genuinely works for people who miss the texture and ritual of baked beans. and at $2.50 a can pre-soaked for the lazy crowd, it's worth trying if you've been craving it. Just go in with eyes open about the oxalate load and lectins, especially if you've had issues with plant antinutrients before. For most carnivore folks, this lands somewhere between "cool occasional indulgence" and "why bother when beef and butter exist," and either answer is fine.
